record.paper_title: Open Problems in Partial Differential Equations Arising from Fluid Dynamics
record.original_question: For the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equations with vortex-sheet initial data, can one obtain classical weak solutions for general initial vortex sheets rather than only measure-valued solutions, and are such solutions unique? Relatedly, for approximate solutions generated by viscous approximation or vortex methods, can energy concentration occur dynamically even when the initial data are strongly convergent in energy norm, and how are these issues connected to concentration-cancellation phenomena?

evidence.quote: Vortex sheets problem and concentration of energy for 2-dimensional Euler equations. Although 2-dimensional smooth inviscid incompressible flows are very well understood to some extent, yet many important questions involving 2-dimensional singular flows remain to be answered.

It is of fundamental importance both physically and mathematically to know whether such a concentration-cancellation occurs to yield the existence of classical weak solution (in contrast to measure-valued solutions) to 2-D Euler equations with general vortex sheets initial data.

Does the same phenomena occur for general vortex sheets initial data? Does energy-concentration occur at all dynamically for such approximate solutions ... ? ... Finally, the uniqueness of weak solutions to the 2-D Euler equations are wildly open except the case where initial vorticity are bounded in the super-norm [52].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equations
   ∂_t u + (u·∇)u + ∇p = 0,   div u = 0,   x ∈ ℝ², t > 0,
with vortex-sheet initial data, i.e. an initial velocity u₀ ∈ L²_loc(ℝ²) that is divergence free and whose vorticity ω₀ = curl u₀ is a finite Radon measure on ℝ² (possibly without a distinguished sign). A weak solution is a divergence-free u ∈ L^∞_t L²_loc satisfying the Euler equations in the sense of distributions; this is called a classical weak solution if the nonlinear term u⊗u is locally integrable and the equations hold in the standard distributional sense (rather than only as a measure-valued solution in the sense of DiPerna–Majda).

Address the following:

(a) For every vortex-sheet initial datum u₀ as above (in particular without any sign assumption on ω₀), does there exist a global-in-time classical weak solution u of the 2D Euler equations with u|_{t=0} = u₀?

(b) Is such a weak solution unique within a natural class (extending Yudovich's uniqueness theorem for ω₀ ∈ L^∞ to vortex-sheet data)?

(c) Let {u^ε} be a family of approximate solutions obtained either by vanishing-viscosity (Navier–Stokes) approximation or by a vortex method, with initial data u₀^ε → u₀ strongly in L²_loc. Determine whether energy concentration can develop dynamically for t > 0 (i.e. whether |u^ε|² can converge in the sense of measures to a limit possessing a singular part supported on a set of Lebesgue measure zero), and characterize the relation of this phenomenon to concentration–cancellation, namely the property that u^ε ⊗ u^ε converges in the sense of distributions to u ⊗ u despite possible loss of strong compactness.
artifact.status_search_result: Existence of (non-classical, convex-integration) admissible weak solutions for vortex-sheet initial data without sign has been established (Mengual–Székelyhidi and follow-ups), and numerical and analytical results show non-uniqueness of weak solutions in this regime. However, the existence of classical weak solutions (as opposed to measure-valued ones) for general vortex-sheet data without sign, the dynamic occurrence of energy concentration for viscous/vortex-method approximations with strongly converging initial energy, and the uniqueness question beyond Yudovich's L^∞ vorticity class remain open.

status_evidence.title: Dissipative Euler Flows for Vortex Sheet Initial Data without Distinguished Sign
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of admissible weak solutions for general (signed) vortex-sheet initial data via convex integration.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of weak (admissible) solutions for vortex-sheet data without sign has been obtained, but these are highly non-classical.

status_evidence.title: Numerical evidence of nonuniqueness in the evolution of vortex sheets
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical calculations support existence of two distinct weak solutions with the same vortex-sheet initial data.
status_evidence.claim: Uniqueness of weak solutions for vortex-sheet data is expected to fail; the problem remains analytically open beyond Yudovich's class.

status_evidence.title: Nonuniqueness of Solutions to the Euler Equations with Vorticity in a Lorentz Space
status_evidence.snippet: Nonuniqueness results extend below L^∞ vorticity.
status_evidence.claim: Uniqueness fails in classes broader than Yudovich's, supporting that the general uniqueness problem is open/negative.

status_evidence.title: Desingularization of vortex sheets for the 2D Euler equations
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on desingularization of vortex sheets for 2D Euler.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research indicates the classical-weak-solution and concentration-cancellation questions for general vortex sheets are still being investigated.
